intro: A first-of-its-kind AI-orchestrated hacking campaign, a cheaper frontier coding model, and bitcoin bracing for a possible Fed hike lead today's edition.

items.headline: OpenAI Opens Agents API in Public Beta, Exposing the Codex Harness
items.summary: OpenAI moved its Agents API into public beta on September 10, giving developers a single API call into the same session orchestration, sandboxing, and multi-agent delegation infrastructure that powers Codex.
items.why: Turns Codex's internal harness into general-purpose agent infrastructure other tools can build on.

items.headline: Cognition Ships SWE-2, Undercutting Fable 5.1 on Cost
items.summary: Cognition released SWE-2, a coding model post-trained from Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, scoring 50.0% on FrontierCode 1.1 (within a point of Claude Fable 5.1) at roughly 64% lower cost; it shipped free in Devin for a month.
items.why: Frontier-level coding performance is getting commoditized outside the largest labs.

items.headline: Hundreds of AI Agents Built on Codex and DeepSeek Ran a Real-World Hacking Campaign
items.summary: GreyNoise documented a campaign in which a Russian-speaking actor used hundreds of autonomous AI agents, built on OpenAI's Codex harness and a DeepSeek model, to compromise at least 440 PaperCut NG/MF print servers across 395 organizations in 48 countries, reaching first remote code execution in under four hours.
items.why: One of the first documented mass cyberattacks orchestrated end-to-end by autonomous AI agents rather than humans.

items.headline: Sakana AI Splits Fugu Into Max and Ultra v2 Orchestration Models
items.summary: Sakana AI released Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2, models that route each task across a pool of other models rather than acting as a single network; Ultra v2 uses a 1M-token-context coordinator to match or beat frontier labs on several benchmarks.
items.why: Suggests orchestrating existing models can rival training ever-larger single ones.

items.headline: OpenAI Pauses ChatGPT Pro Sign-Ups as Astra Demand Outstrips Capacity
items.summary: OpenAI temporarily halted new sign-ups for its $200/month ChatGPT Pro tier, citing unprecedented demand for its Astra model, which the company has separately classified as its first to cross a 'Critical' cybersecurity capability threshold.
items.why: Ties commercial demand directly to a model OpenAI itself flags as its riskiest yet.

items.headline: Microsoft Makes Rust a Tier-1 Language Internally
items.summary: Microsoft classified Rust as a tier-1 engineering language on September 11, putting it alongside C++, C#, and TypeScript with a paved path to production, MSVC-backend interoperability, and the same hardening and compliance tooling as its C++ stack.
items.why: Signals a bet on Rust to cut memory-safety bugs, which Microsoft says cause roughly 70% of Windows CVEs.

items.headline: JDK 27 Locks Feature Set Ahead of September 15 Release
items.summary: JDK 27 entered its final rampdown with nine JEPs frozen, making G1 the default garbage collector everywhere, adding post-quantum hybrid key exchange for TLS 1.3, and turning on compact object headers by default; general availability is set for September 15.
items.why: First JDK release to ship post-quantum TLS support by default.

items.headline: Bitcoin Holds Near $77K as Fed Rate-Hike Odds Jump to Roughly 87%
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $77,000 as markets priced in a roughly 87% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates at its September 16 meeting, up sharply from about 70% before this week's hotter-than-expected August CPI print.
items.why: A hike, not a cut, would reverse earlier-2026 rate expectations and is the main overhang on price into next week.

items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs Extend Outflow Streak to Four Days as Capital Rotates to Ether
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a fourth consecutive day of net outflows on September 11, a reversal from the roughly $987 million they took in the prior week, while spot Ether ETFs pulled in $216 million the same day.
items.why: A four-day reversal from near-billion-dollar buying is a notable shift in institutional positioning.

items.headline: Nasdaq Invests $100M in Kraken Parent Payward at $21B Valuation
items.summary: Nasdaq's venture arm invested $100 million in Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, valuing it at $21 billion and expanding a partnership to bring tokenized Nasdaq-listed stocks to Kraken users by 2027.
items.why: One of the largest strategic bets yet linking a legacy exchange operator to a crypto platform.
